# Plugin protocol

A plugin is a binary kapi discovers, launches, and talks to over one of three
transports. This page describes the contract both sides hold to.

## Discovery

Roots are searched in order, and the first manifest wins.

Results are cached as JSON, keyed by each root's directory mtime. The cache is
rejected when the binary's cache version changes.

## Standard verbs

Every plugin binary answers these, regardless of which transports it declares:

```
<binary> version           # print the plugin's version, exit 0
<binary> doctor            # self-check, exit 0 when healthy (only if selfcheck)
```

`version` confirms an installed binary matches its manifest. `doctor` backs the
plugin health check; a plugin that bundles native libraries declares the
capability and confirms those resolve.

An **unrecognised** first argument must exit non-zero. A catch-all dispatcher
silently absorbs verbs added by a later protocol revision instead of failing
visibly, so this is a required rule rather than a style preference.

## The three transports

A manifest's capability sections determine which transports kapi uses. A plugin
may declare any subset.

| Capability section | Transport | Invocation                    |
| ------------------ | --------- | ----------------------------- |
| `commands`         | argv      | `<binary> <verb> [flags]`     |
| `formats`          | stream    | `<binary> serve --stdio`      |
| `tools`            | gRPC      | `<binary> daemon --port 0`    |

### Argv

The simplest transport: kapi runs the binary once per invocation and reads its
exit code.

```bash
kapi plugins run example -- --help
```

### Stream

kapi writes length-prefixed frames on stdin and reads them from stdout. Frames
carry the content model, so a stream plugin sees the same blocks a native
format reader emits.

## Failure modes

A plugin that exits non-zero fails the step that called it. A plugin that
writes malformed frames fails the read with the offending frame's offset, which
is the only way a truncated stream is distinguishable from a short one.
